title.raw: Pending Criminal Case or FIR: Will It Affect Your Job, Background Verification, Passport or Visa?
title.rendered: Pending Criminal Case or FIR: Will It Affect Your Job, Background Verification, Passport or Visa?

content.raw:
In short: A pending criminal case does not automatically cost you your job, passport or visa, but it can surface in background checks and police verification, and it often means you need a court's permission before getting a passport or travelling abroad. The usual approach is to disclose accurately where you are asked, apply to the court for permission or modification of bail conditions when travel is needed, and, where the facts support it, consider an early discharge or quashing. Concealing a case usually causes more harm than the case itself.

What actually shows up in BGV and police verification

People often mix up three different records:

RecordWho sees itWhen it appears
FIR at the police stationPolice; may surface in police verification for passports, PCC or some government jobsFrom registration of the FIR
Court case recordsAnyone searching eCourts by name, including many private BGV agenciesOnce a charge-sheet or complaint is filed and the court registers the case
Police Clearance Certificate (PCC)Foreign employers, embassies, immigration authoritiesWhen you apply; police verification checks for pending cases

Private employers and BGV agencies usually search court databases and sometimes verify addresses with the local police. An FIR that is still under investigation may not appear in a court search, but a case filed in court generally will, because court records are public. How deep the check goes depends on the employer and the agency's contract.

Accurate disclosure matters. If a form asks whether any criminal case is pending against you, a false "no" can become a separate problem. For government employment, the Supreme Court in Avtar Singh v. Union of India (2016) held that suppression or false information in verification forms can itself justify action, while also saying employers must consider the nature of the case and the circumstances. Private employers follow their own policies, but the same logic applies: an honest answer, with documents showing the case's status, is easier to explain than a discovered concealment.

  • Answer exactly what is asked. "Pending case" and "conviction" are different questions.
  • Keep copies of the FIR, your bail or anticipatory bail order and the latest case status ready.
  • Being named in an FIR or being on bail is not a finding of guilt. You can say that without overstating your case.

Passport: applying or renewing with a pending case

Under Section 6(2)(f) of the Passports Act, 1967, a passport may be refused if criminal proceedings against the applicant are pending before a court in India. A government notification allows a passport to be issued in such cases if the court where the case is pending permits it. In practice this is often called the court "NOC" or permission route.

Practical steps

  1. Check the stage of the case. If only an FIR exists and nothing is pending in court, the position is different from a case where a charge-sheet has been filed. Police verification may still mention the FIR.
  2. Apply to the court where the case is pending for permission to apply for or renew the passport. The application explains why it is needed (job, family, studies) and offers undertakings, such as attending every date and informing the court of travel.
  3. Get a certified copy of the order. The court may limit the period of validity or add conditions.
  4. Disclose the case in the passport application and attach the court's order. The Regional Passport Office in Pune and the police verification will rely on the information you give.

The Supreme Court has recognised, since Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978), that the right to travel abroad is part of personal liberty under Article 21 and can be restricted only by a fair procedure established by law. That is why courts weigh your need to travel against the need to secure your attendance at trial.

This question comes up often in matrimonial cases. A pending 498A case (now Sections 85 and 86 BNS) does not by itself bar renewal, but the court permission route above is generally needed.

Travelling abroad while on bail or anticipatory bail

First, read your bail order carefully. Common conditions include:

  • "Shall not leave India without prior permission of the court"
  • "Shall surrender passport" or "shall deposit passport with the police station"
  • "Shall attend the police station" on specified days

If there is a travel condition, you need permission from the court before you travel. The application usually gives the purpose, dates, destination and address abroad, a copy of the ticket or invitation letter, and undertakings to return and attend. Courts sometimes ask for an additional surety or a deposit. Our page on anticipatory bail conditions explains how these conditions are usually worded and read.

If your order has no travel condition, check with your lawyer anyway. Upcoming dates still need attendance or exemption, and missing them can lead to a warrant. See how NBW cancellation works.

Changing bail conditions: weekly attendance (haajri), travel, city change

Bail conditions are not necessarily permanent. A weekly or monthly attendance at the police station (haajri), a ban on leaving the district, or a passport deposit can be modified on an application to the court that granted the bail. For anticipatory bail, that may be the Sessions Court in Pune or the Bombay High Court in Mumbai, depending on which court passed the order.

What courts usually consider:

  • How long you have complied with the existing conditions
  • Whether investigation is complete or a charge-sheet has been filed
  • The reason: a new job, a transfer, studies, or a family need, supported by documents
  • Whether the complainant or prosecution shows a real risk of absconding or tampering with evidence

More detail is on our pages for bail applications and anticipatory bail.

After quashing, discharge or acquittal

A favourable order ends the case, but it does not remove the record from every database. Court websites may still show the case as "disposed", and old police records may still mention the FIR.

  • Keep certified copies of the final order and, where relevant, the High Court order.
  • Answer BGV questions accurately: "A case was registered in [year]; it was quashed/I was discharged/acquitted on [date]", with the order attached.
  • Check for appeals: the State or complainant may challenge an acquittal or discharge within the limitation period. Your lawyer can tell you whether one has been filed.

When to consider quashing or discharge early

If the case is affecting a job offer or travel, it is worth asking whether it can be brought to an end earlier than a full trial.

  • Quashing is sought before the Bombay High Court under Section 528 BNSS (formerly 482 CrPC), either on the merits or on settlement in suitable cases. See FIR quashing.
  • Discharge is sought before the trial court after the charge-sheet is filed, if the material does not disclose sufficient grounds. See discharge applications.

Time and cost: neither is quick or certain. A High Court petition can take months or longer depending on listing, and a discharge application depends on when the trial court hears it. The cost depends on the court, the volume of papers, the number of hearings and whether the other side contests. A lawyer can give you an estimate after reading the papers. If you are living abroad, our page for NRIs facing criminal cases in India covers working through a power of attorney and remote hearings.

Frequently asked questions

Can I renew my passport if a 498A case is pending?

Generally yes, with the permission of the court where the case is pending. You apply to that court explaining why you need the passport, the court may impose conditions, and you then submit its order with your passport application while disclosing the case.

Will my employer find out about an FIR?

It depends on how thorough the background check is. An FIR under investigation may not appear in court searches, but once a case is filed in court it is publicly searchable by name. If the employer asks directly, answer accurately and keep documents ready.

Can I take a job abroad while on bail?

Only if your bail conditions allow it, or the court permits it. If the order restricts travel or required you to deposit your passport, apply to the court that granted bail for permission or modification before you accept a joining date.

Does an anticipatory bail order stop me travelling?

It depends on the conditions. Many anticipatory bail orders require prior permission before leaving India or ask you to cooperate with investigation on call. Read the order, and apply for permission if it contains such a condition.

Can I get a Police Clearance Certificate with a pending case?

Police verification for a PCC checks for pending cases, and a pending case is likely to be reported. Whether a certificate is issued, and in what form, depends on the authorities. Having court permission and the case papers ready helps you explain the position to an employer or embassy.

Will a disposed case still show in background checks?

It may, because court records remain online as disposed cases. Keep certified copies of the final order and describe the outcome accurately when asked.

This article explains the law in general terms and is not legal advice. Every case depends on its own facts.
